profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting between a programme lead at a Europe-based sustainability institute and a research operations coordinator at a South Asia-based university center to organize a new international interdisciplinary pilot project inspired by Francesco di Castri's 1978 article on planning international interdisciplinary research. The initiative will connect ecologists, public policy scholars, and data scientists across India, Kenya, and France to prepare for a philanthropic funder's informal pre-consultation on a future biosphere resilience call. The agenda is to decide what must be produced over the next four weeks, who will draft and coordinate each part, how input from the cross-country collaborators will be gathered, and what exactly needs to be 'ready for circulation' before the pre-consultation. The expected outcome is a shared near-term plan for deliverables, responsibilities, and review steps, while subtle but consequential differences in assumptions remain unspoken.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.role: Programme Lead for Global Research Initiatives
members.expertise: International research strategy, interdisciplinary consortium building, environmental policy programmes
members.background: Lena works at a Paris-based sustainability institute and has led several multinational scoping exercises that begin with brief framing documents used to open conversations with external funders before a full proposal is assembled.
members.private_state: She wants a polished, externally presentable package quickly so she can use the pre-consultation to secure early interest from the funder, and she is worried that formal coordination steps will dilute momentum and make the project look immature.
hidden_assumptions: Preparing the concept note for the pre-consultation means producing the document that will actually be shared with the funder during or immediately after the call.
The pilot team means one named lead per country node plus the methods adviser, with broader disciplinary contributors consulted informally through those leads.
A circulatable draft is ready once the narrative is coherent, the problem framing is persuasive, and provisional partner roles are intelligible even if operational details are still placeholders.
When someone says the draft is ready for circulation, the next circulation step is outward to the funder-facing conversation unless someone explicitly says internal clearance is required.

members.name: Samir Banerjee
members.expertise: Academic project setup, multi-institution coordination, research administration, workshop logistics
members.background: Samir works at a Bengaluru-based university center that routinely translates early research ideas into internally reviewable planning files before any materials are shown outside the institution or its formal partners.
members.private_state: He wants to protect the university and partner institutions from reputational risk by ensuring that anything associated with them has enough structure and review behind it, and he is concerned about creating expectations with external funders before internal stakeholders have seen the materials.
hidden_assumptions: Preparing the concept note for the pre-consultation means assembling the internal package the team needs in order to enter that meeting well-prepared, not necessarily the exact document that will be handed to the funder.
The pilot team includes the wider interdisciplinary working group already named in exploratory calls across the three countries, because interdisciplinary buy-in is part of the pilot itself.

A circulatable draft is ready only when the implementation outline, contributor list, and indicative resourcing are stable enough to be distributed across institutions without generating contradictory follow-up questions.

When someone says a draft is ready for circulation, the immediate next step is circulation to the university grants office and institutional stakeholders for clearance before anything external happens.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to prepare the concept note for the pre-consultation
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to 'prepare the concept note for the pre-consultation.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the concept note is the external-facing document meant to be shown to the philanthropic funder as the basis for the pre-consultation discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the concept note is the team's internal briefing document that prepares the consortium for the pre-consultation, while any external-facing material may be derived from it later.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds perfectly standard because both see the concept note as linked to the same upcoming meeting, and neither expects that the apparently minor difference between 'for the meeting' and 'for the funder' needs to be spelled out.

misalignment_points.topic: Who counts as the pilot team
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss getting feedback from the 'pilot team' before wider sharing.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the pilot team is the small core coordination group: the India, Kenya, and France leads plus one cross-cutting methods adviser.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the pilot team is the broader interdisciplinary set of researchers already drawn into the exploratory conversations, including ecology, policy, and data contributors at each institution.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have heard the same label used across earlier calls, and because everyone involved is in some sense part of the pilot effort, the category boundary feels socially obvious rather than something that would normally be itemized.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a circulatable draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need a 'circulatable draft' before the pre-consultation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the draft is circulatable once it has a strong narrative arc, a clear three-country rationale, and enough specificity to sound credible in an external conversation even if tables, staffing details, and budget placeholders are unfinished.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the draft is circulatable only when the implementation outline, named contributors, and indicative resource lines are stable enough that multiple institutions can review it without misreading provisional elements as settled commitments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Circulatable draft is a familiar coordination shorthand that signals stage of progress rather than a precise threshold, so each person hears shared momentum while silently applying their own quality standard.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'ready for circulation' triggers as the next process step
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the first version should be 'ready for circulation' next week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes that once the first version is ready for circulation, she can send it directly to the funder's programme officer or use it as the leave-behind document immediately after the pre-consultation call.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes that once the first version is ready for circulation, it should first go to his university's grants office and selected institutional stakeholders for a light internal clearance round before any external sharing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both agree on the same immediate milestone and use the same process language, but 'circulation' naturally sounds like a routine administrative step whose audience is already obvious, so neither thinks to specify the route.

turns.inner_thought: We need to use this meeting to lock a short runway. For me, preparing the concept note for the pre-consultation means getting the actual funder-facing document into shape fast enough to use in the call or send right after it. If we let this become a sprawling coordination exercise, we'll lose the chance to create early enthusiasm with the programme officer.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making the time, Samir. I'd like us to use this meeting to map the next four weeks clearly so we can prepare the concept note for the pre-consultation with the philanthropic funder.

turns.inner_thought: Agreed. The concept note for the pre-consultation should prepare the team properly for that meeting, which to me means a reliable internal planning document first. If people across the institutions feel grounded before the conversation, we reduce the risk of overpromising or creating confusion later.
turns.utterance: That would be useful. If we structure it well, the concept note should give everyone a confident basis for the pre-consultation.

turns.inner_thought: I'll take the front-end writing myself so the tone stays sharp and persuasive. Then I only want quick comments from the core pilot team as I define it: one lead in each country and the methods adviser. There's no reason to open the draft to the wider group before the core story is coherent.
turns.utterance: My thought is that I draft the framing sections first—the rationale, the overall ambition, and the three-country logic—and then we get quick comments from the pilot team before any wider sharing.

turns.inner_thought: Good, and I can make sure the broader pilot team is actually reflected early: ecology, policy, and data people across the three-country set. If their perspectives come in now, we avoid a situation where later reviewers feel the pilot was defined without them.
turns.utterance: I can help there by coordinating pilot team input across the ecology, policy, and data people, so the draft picks up those perspectives early without becoming chaotic.

turns.inner_thought: For a circulatable draft, I do not need a fully engineered project file. What matters is a compelling narrative arc, a clear reason for the India-Kenya-France structure, and a few biosphere examples that make it tangible. Placeholders are fine at this stage as long as the document reads credibly.
turns.utterance: For the first pass, I think we just need the core rationale, the three-country structure, and a few example biosphere sites in place for it to become a circulatable draft.

turns.inner_thought: That won't be enough for my sense of circulatable if it has to move across institutions. I'll make sure the implementation structure, contributor picture, and rough resourcing are settled enough that people do not read provisional elements as commitments or gaps.
turns.utterance: That works. I'll make sure the implementation structure is solid enough that the same draft is comfortable to circulate.

turns.inner_thought: If we can get a first version next week, I can keep momentum with the funder. Ready for circulation next week should mean I have something coherent enough to support the pre-consultation and very likely use directly in the funder-facing exchange unless someone explicitly stops that.
turns.utterance: In that case, let's aim to have a first version ready for circulation next week so it can support the pre-consultation preparation.

turns.inner_thought: That's feasible if I can move it through the internal checks immediately after. Once it's ready for circulation, I want to send it through the grants office and the relevant institutional stakeholders so we can gather comments quickly and enter the meeting in a safer position.
turns.utterance: Next week should be manageable. Once it's ready for circulation, I'll route it through the necessary review channels and collect comments quickly.

turns.inner_thought: Fine. As long as Samir is basically collecting input from the three country leads and feeding that into a tight pilot team review, this should stay contained. I need to hold the opening narrative so the voice remains polished and convincing.
turns.utterance: Then I'll take responsibility for the opening narrative, and perhaps you could pull input from the country leads and fold that into the pilot team review.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, I'll use that review round to stabilize the draft with the broader interdisciplinary group so it is robust enough for cross-institutional circulation. The point is to have enough structure behind it that the external conversations are well prepared rather than improvised.
turns.utterance: I can do that. That review round should make the draft stable enough for circulation so we're fully prepared for the external conversations.

turns.inner_thought: Good, we seem aligned: produce the concept note for the pre-consultation, get a quick pilot team pass, and have a circulatable version next week. That should give me what I need to present the idea with confidence and keep the opportunity moving.
turns.utterance: Good. So the plan is that we prepare the concept note for the pre-consultation, get pilot team feedback on the first pass, and have a circulatable version next week.

turns.inner_thought: I'll send a tracker that quietly embeds the review sequence I have in mind, along with drafting responsibilities. If that is documented early, we can keep the institutions comfortable and avoid any surprises once the package starts moving.
turns.utterance: I'll send over a task tracker this afternoon with drafting owners and the circulation steps so the package moves smoothly.
